ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a 5×5 grid. The upper-left square is marked with ×, and the squares around it marked with · include not only the usually adjacent right, lower, and lower-right squares, but also the squares that “wrap around” through the boundary to the rightmost column and the bottom row. This shows that the grid is understood modulo 5, and is a toroidal grid whose top and bottom, left and right are both connected end to end; the neighborhood of each point is a 3×3 region modulo 5. Reasoning: According to the meaning of the problem, two different points (a,b),(x,y) are adjacent if and only if the row difference a-x and the column difference b-y both respectively belong to -1,0,1 mod 5. Let the number of × placed in row i be r_i, with row numbers calculated modulo 5. First look at a single row: in the same row, if two columns differ by 0, ±1 mod 5, then they are adjacent, so the selected columns in one row must be an independent set on the 5-cycle, and at most only 2 can be selected, hence r_i ≤ 2. More strongly, for any two adjacent rows i and i+1, there is r_i + r_{i+1} ≤ 2. The proof is as follows: if row i has 2 ×, these two column positions must be separated by 2 on the 5-cycle; each × will forbid the same column and the left and right adjacent columns in the next row, together covering all 5 columns of the next row, so r_{i+1}=0. If row i has 1 ×, suppose its column is c, then row i+1 can place only in the two columns c+2 and c-2 at distance 2 from c; but modulo 5 these two columns differ by 4, namely differ by -1, so they are adjacent to each other, and at most only 1 can be selected. Therefore there is always r_i+r_{i+1}≤2. Sum the five inequalities r_i+r_{i+1}≤2 for i=0,1,2,3,4, obtaining 2(r_0+r_1+r_2+r_3+r_4)≤10. If the total number is N, then 2N≤10, so N≤5. Below construct 5 feasible ×: take the points (i,2i mod 5), namely (0,0),(1,2),(2,4),(3,1),(4,3). The column difference between adjacent rows is 2 or -2 mod 5, which does not belong to -1,0,1, so they are not adjacent; the row difference of non-adjacent rows itself does not belong to -1,0,1, so they are also not adjacent. Therefore 5 can be placed. Therefore the maximum number is 5.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a 5-by-5 toroidal grid: the marked x is in a corner, and the dots around it include cells wrapping across the top/bottom and left/right edges, showing that adjacency is a wrapped 3-by-3 neighborhood. From the text, use the modular definition of adjacency. Let r_i be the number of x's in row i, with row indices taken mod 5. In one row, selected columns form an independent set on a 5-cycle, so r_i <= 2. Prove the stronger local bound r_i + r_{i+1} <= 2 for every adjacent pair of rows: if row i has two x's, their column-neighborhoods cover all five columns of row i+1, so row i+1 is empty; if row i has one x, row i+1 can use only the two columns at cyclic distance 2 from it, and those two columns are adjacent to each other, so row i+1 has at most one x. Summing the five inequalities r_i + r_{i+1} <= 2 gives 2N <= 10, so N <= 5. Then exhibit 5 x's, for example at (i, 2i mod 5) for i = 0,1,2,3,4; consecutive rows differ by 2 columns, and nonconsecutive rows are already nonadjacent in row coordinate. Hence the maximum is 5.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个 5×5 方格。左上角方格标有 ×，而它周围标有 · 的方格不仅包括通常相邻的右边、下边、右下方格，还包括通过边界“绕回”到最右列和最下行的方格。这说明该网格按模 5 理解，是一个上下、左右都首尾相接的环面网格；每个点的邻域是按模 5 的 3×3 区域。

推理：根据题意，两个不同点 (a,b),(x,y) 相邻当且仅当行差 a-x 和列差 b-y 都分别属于 -1,0,1 mod 5。设第 i 行中放置的 × 的个数为 r_i，行号按模 5 计算。

先看单独一行：同一行中，若两列相差 0, ±1 mod 5，则相邻，所以一行中被选的列必须是在 5-循环上的独立集，最多只能选 2 个，因此 r_i ≤ 2。

更强地，对于任意相邻两行 i 和 i+1，有 r_i + r_{i+1} ≤ 2。证明如下：如果第 i 行有 2 个 ×，这两个列位置在 5-循环上必须相隔 2；每个 × 会禁止下一行中同列及左右相邻列，共同覆盖下一行全部 5 列，所以 r_{i+1}=0。若第 i 行有 1 个 ×，设其列为 c，则第 i+1 行只能在与 c 距离为 2 的两列 c+2 和 c-2 上放置；但在模 5 下这两列相差 4，即相差 -1，所以它们彼此相邻，最多只能选 1 个。因此总有 r_i+r_{i+1}≤2。

将五个不等式 r_i+r_{i+1}≤2 对 i=0,1,2,3,4 求和，得到 2(r_0+r_1+r_2+r_3+r_4)≤10。若总数为 N，则 2N≤10，所以 N≤5。

下面构造 5 个可行的 ×：取点 (i,2i mod 5)，即 (0,0),(1,2),(2,4),(3,1),(4,3)。相邻两行之间列差为 2 或 -2 mod 5，不属于 -1,0,1，因此不相邻；非相邻行的行差本身就不属于 -1,0,1，因此也不相邻。所以可以放 5 个。

因此最大数量是 5。

method.method_draft: First describe the picture as a 5-by-5 grid on a torus: the x in the corner has dot-neighbors across the ordinary edges and also across the wraparound edges, matching modular adjacency. From the text, model the allowed conflict graph: vertices are cells (a,b), and two cells conflict exactly when in each coordinate they are equal or adjacent on the cycle C5. Thus the conflict graph is the strong product C5 ⊠ C5. An admissible placement is an independent set in this graph. Use the Lovasz theta bound: alpha(G) <= theta(G), theta is multiplicative under strong products, and theta(C5) = sqrt(5). Therefore alpha(C5 ⊠ C5) <= theta(C5 ⊠ C5) = theta(C5)^2 = 5. For attainability, place x's on the slope-2 modular line {(i, 2i mod 5): i in Z5}; any two chosen points differ either by a row distance ±2, or, if the row distance is ±1, by a column distance ±2, so they are not adjacent. Therefore 5 is achievable and optimal.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个 5×5 方格，左上角方格内有一个 ×。带点的方格不仅包括普通意义上靠近左上角的相邻方格，还包括跨过上边界、左边界后在另一侧出现的方格；这说明网格按模 5 环绕，也就是在二维环面上考虑邻接。

推理：把每个方格看作顶点 (a,b)∈Z_5^2。两个不同方格冲突当且仅当两个坐标差都属于 {-1,0,1} mod 5。也就是说，冲突图是 C5 ⊠ C5，即两个 5-环的强积。可放置的 × 集合就是该冲突图中的独立集。

用 Lovasz theta 数给上界：独立数满足 α(G)≤θ(G)，且 θ 对强积可乘；又 θ(C5)=√5。因此
α(C5 ⊠ C5) ≤ θ(C5 ⊠ C5)=θ(C5)^2=(√5)^2=5。
所以最多不能超过 5 个。

再给出可达到的 5 个：放在模 5 斜率为 2 的直线上
{(i,2i mod 5): i∈Z5}，例如 (0,0),(1,2),(2,4),(3,1),(4,3)。任取两点，它们的行差若为 ±1，则列差为 ±2；行差若为 ±2，则已经不是相邻行。因此任意两点都不相邻。故 5 个可以达到，且由上界知最优。

用 Lovasz theta 数给上界：独立数满足 α(G)≤θ(G)，且 θ 对强积可乘；又 θ(C5)=√5。因此
α(C5 ⊠ C5) ≤ θ(C5 ⊠ C5)=θ(C5)^2=(√5)^2=5。
所以最多不能超过 5 个。

再给出可达到的 5 个：放在模 5 斜率为 2 的直线上
{(i,2i mod 5): i∈Z5}，例如 (0,0),(1,2),(2,4),(3,1),(4,3)。任取两点，它们的行差若为 ±1，则列差为 ±2；行差若为 ±2，则已经不是相邻行。因此任意两点都不相邻。故 5 个可以达到，且由上界知最优。

raw_record.original_question: Consider the $5\times 5$ grid $Z^2_5 = \{(a, b) : 0 \le a, b \le 4\}$. Say that two points $(a, b)$, $(x, y)$ are adjacent if $a - x \equiv -1, 0, 1 \pmod{5}$ and $b - y \equiv -1, 0, 1 \pmod{5}$. For example, in the diagram, all of the squares marked with $\cdot$ are adjacent to the square marked with $\times$. What is the largest number of $\times$ that can be placed on the grid such that no two are adjacent?
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The figure is a 5×5 grid. The upper-left square is marked with ×, and the squares around it marked with · include not only the usually adjacent right, lower, and lower-right squares, but also the squares that “wrap around” through the boundary to the rightmost column and the bottom row. This shows that the grid is understood modulo 5, and is a toroidal grid whose top and bottom, left and right are both connected end to end; the neighborhood of each point is a 3×3 region modulo 5.

Reasoning: According to the meaning of the problem, two different points (a,b),(x,y) are adjacent if and only if the row difference a-x and the column difference b-y both respectively belong to -1,0,1 mod 5. Let the number of × placed in row i be r_i, with row numbers calculated modulo 5.

First look at a single row: in the same row, if two columns differ by 0, ±1 mod 5, then they are adjacent, so the selected columns in one row must be an independent set on the 5-cycle, and at most only 2 can be selected, hence r_i ≤ 2.

More strongly, for any two adjacent rows i and i+1, there is r_i + r_{i+1} ≤ 2. The proof is as follows: if row i has 2 ×, these two column positions must be separated by 2 on the 5-cycle; each × will forbid the same column and the left and right adjacent columns in the next row, together covering all 5 columns of the next row, so r_{i+1}=0. If row i has 1 ×, suppose its column is c, then row i+1 can place only in the two columns c+2 and c-2 at distance 2 from c; but modulo 5 these two columns differ by 4, namely differ by -1, so they are adjacent to each other, and at most only 1 can be selected. Therefore there is always r_i+r_{i+1}≤2.

Sum the five inequalities r_i+r_{i+1}≤2 for i=0,1,2,3,4, obtaining 2(r_0+r_1+r_2+r_3+r_4)≤10. If the total number is N, then 2N≤10, so N≤5.

Below construct 5 feasible ×: take the points (i,2i mod 5), namely (0,0),(1,2),(2,4),(3,1),(4,3). The column difference between adjacent rows is 2 or -2 mod 5, which does not belong to -1,0,1, so they are not adjacent; the row difference of non-adjacent rows itself does not belong to -1,0,1, so they are also not adjacent. Therefore 5 can be placed.

Therefore the maximum number is 5.
